original_question: For integers q >= p >= r >= 2, how can one characterize the graphs in G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) that have the largest spectral radius?
target_in_paper: The theta-graph specialization of the introductory almost-bipartite extremal problem: Conjecture 1.1 with F = theta_{r,p,q}, made explicit in Proposition 1.2 and then settled in Theorem 1.3.
correct_elements: The draft correctly identifies the forbidden graph family theta_{r,p,q}, keeps the parameter range q >= p >= r >= 2, uses the paper’s notation G(m,F), and asks for the spectral-extremal graphs, i.e. those with largest spectral radius.
missing_details: The paper’s theta graph theta_{r,p,q} must be defined explicitly as the graph formed by three internally disjoint paths of lengths r, p, q joining the same two distinct endpoints.
The family G(m,F) needs to be defined as the set of F-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices.
The spectral radius must be identified as the adjacency spectral radius lambda(G), i.e. the largest eigenvalue of the adjacency matrix A(G).
The paper’s introductory formulation is asymptotic: it is not for every m, but for all sufficiently large integers m.
The paper’s formulation is about determining the unique extremal graph, not merely describing a possibly non-unique collection of maximizers.
Your draft does not indicate that the theta-graph question is presented in the paper as a specialization of a more general conjectural/extremal statement for almost-bipartite graphs.
If one wants the fully paper-faithful formulation, the candidate extremal split graph singled out by the Proposition 1.2 reformulation should be named explicitly.
refined_question: Let theta_{r,p,q} be the graph obtained by joining two distinct vertices with three internally disjoint paths of lengths r, p, and q, where q >= p >= r >= 2. Let G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) denote the family of theta_{r,p,q}-free graphs with exactly m edges and no isolated vertices, and let lambda(G) be the spectral radius of the adjacency matrix of G. For all sufficiently large integers m, determine the unique graph G in G(m, theta_{r,p,q}) that maximizes lambda(G).
equivalent_formulation: Does Conjecture 1.1 hold in the special case F = theta_{r,p,q}, equivalently as reformulated for theta graphs in Proposition 1.2?
justification: Your draft is aimed at the paper’s introductory theta-graph specialization of the general almost-bipartite edge-spectral-Turan problem. The introduction first states the general conjectural formulation (Conjecture 1.1), then isolates the theta-graph case in Proposition 1.2, and finally records its resolution in Theorem 1.3. So the nearest paper-faithful target is not a broader question about arbitrary forbidden subgraphs, but exactly the theta_{r,p,q} case, with the paper’s own ambient notation G(m,F), adjacency spectral radius lambda(G), asymptotic quantifier 'for all sufficiently large m', and uniqueness of the extremal graph. The draft already captures the correct forbidden family and extremal objective, but it omits these stand-alone definitional and quantificational details that the paper treats as part of the formal statement.
